about.title: Duarte Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: When someone gets hurt on the job in Duarte, most people assume workers' compensation is the only path forward — and often it is, since California treats workers' comp as the exclusive remedy against an employer regardless of fault. But that's not the whole picture. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to the injury, a separate claim against that third party may be possible alongside any workers' comp benefits. This matters in a city like Duarte, where industrial and logistics work near the I-210 corridor and commercial stretches of Huntington Drive often involves multiple companies and contractors on a single site. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself — we connect injured workers with an independent attorney, free of charge, who can sort through the layers and explain what options actually apply to your situation.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Independent Attorney First

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Whole Story
items.desc: California generally makes workers' comp the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party — like a subcontractor or equipment maker — can still be pursued separately.

items.title: Deadlines Move Fast
items.desc: You typically have just 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and any third-party injury claim carries its own two-year filing deadline under California law.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report an injury or pursue a claim, so raising the issue shouldn't cost you your job.

items.question: If I already filed a workers' comp claim in Duarte, can I still pursue something else?
items.answer: Yes, in some cases. Workers' comp usually covers your employer's liability, but if a third party — like a contractor working alongside your employer or an equipment supplier — contributed to your injury, a separate claim may be possible. An independent attorney can review the details and tell you whether that applies to you.

items.question: What if my injury happened driving for work near I-210 or Huntington Drive?
items.answer: Work-related driving injuries can get complicated because they may involve your employer, another driver, and possibly a vehicle manufacturer. These cases often involve overlapping claims, so it helps to have someone review the specifics rather than assume workers' comp is the only remedy.

items.question: My employer told me not to report the injury — is that legal?
items.answer: No. California law protects workers from retaliation for reporting a workplace injury, and you generally have 30 days to make that report. If you're being discouraged or pressured, an independent attorney can advise you on your rights and next steps.
